2609.17755.title: Evolution of US Oral Political Language
2609.17755.paper_summary: The analysis of US political language is usually based on the written form (e.g. presidential addresses) or posts broadcasted on various social networks. Oral production, however, which is even more frequent, can better reveal the style and mode of thinking of the speaker. This study covers this mode of linguistic communication by considering 19 candidates from the presidential elections between 1960 to 2024. Our main research objectives are to disclose the main trends hidden in those presidential debates. Do we observe a clear simplification of the US political language over time? Does Trump have poor language compared to the other candidates? Do unusual stylistic features occur only with a single, specific president? Moreover, can we detect a pattern explaining the success or failure of some nominees? Over time, this study demonstrates a significant reduction in political language complexity, a decrease of the mean sentence length, and a noteworthy decline of complex terms. Moreover, the emotional tone increases over the decades, while logical and rational thinking tends to lessen.
2609.17755.paper_summary_zh: 美國政治語言的分析通常基於書面形式（例如總統演說）或在各種社交網絡上廣播的帖子。然而，口語表達更為頻繁，能更好地揭示講者的風格和思維模式。本研究通過考慮1960年至2024年之間的19位候選人來涵蓋這種語言交流模式。我們的主要研究目標是揭示那些總統辯論中隱藏的主要趨勢。我們是否觀察到美國政治語言隨時間的明顯簡化？特朗普的語言是否比其他候選人差？不尋常的風格特徵是否僅出現在某位特定的總統身上？此外，我們能否檢測到解釋某些提名人成功或失敗的模式？隨著時間的推移，本研究顯示政治語言的複雜性顯著降低，平均句子長度減少，複雜術語的顯著下降。此外，情感語調在幾十年中增加，而邏輯和理性思維則趨向減少。
